title: Sévéane TP (Korelio) for opticians: professional portal, coverage approval, statuses, and payment
metaDescription: Sévéane TP (Korelio) for opticians: access to the professional portal, optical coverage approval, statuses, and payment. The steps to unblock a file at the counter.
contentHtml:
Sévéane TP requests are entered on korelio.com, or on seveane.com for partners in the Sévéane network. Sévéane is a care network born from an agreement between Groupama and PRO BTP, as PRO BTP explains on its partners page. Its third-party payment (tiers payant: the patient pays nothing upfront, insurers pay the provider directly) is managed by Korelio, the services network PRO BTP created for its exchanges with healthcare professionals.

For an optician, it comes down to three steps. Read the customer’s Korelio card, with the code “OPTI”. Enter the request on the right portal. Bill with the “Facturer” (Invoice) button.

This page brings together what Sévéane, Korelio, and PRO BTP publish, plus what our agents observe when entering files on these portals. It is part of our overview of third-party payment portals, where every platform follows the same outline.

Key takeaways
  • The professional portal for Sévéane third-party payment is korelio.com, or seveane.com for partners in the Sévéane network. Korelio manages this third-party payment.
  • The Sévéane network is closed (a limited number of opticians per area, current contract running from 2024 to 2027). Outside the network, the Korelio optical agreement opens up third-party payment.
  • Logging in requires a username, a password, and a code received by email. On seveane.com, a rejected username shows the same message as a real outage.
  • A validated coverage approval is billed with the “Facturer” button, with no paper invoice. It then moves to the “FACTUREE” (Invoiced) status.

What is Sévéane (Korelio), and which insurers go through it?

Sévéane is the care network of Groupama and PRO BTP; Korelio manages its third-party payment. Its third-party payment card confirms the policyholder’s coverage rights and guarantees reimbursement by Korelio.

In terms of structure, Sévéane is now a simplified joint-stock company (SAS) owned in equal shares by Groupama Assurances Mutuelles and BTP-Prévoyance, registered in May 2022. On January 1, 2023, it absorbed the Sévéane economic interest group (GIE), created in 2010. These details appear in the 2024 call for applications for opticians in the Sévéane network. The same document states that BTP-Prévoyance acts on behalf of the PRO BTP Group and of all the organizations that use Korelio optical third-party payment.

Korelio third-party payment therefore does not only cover PRO BTP members. On its partners page, Korelio lists the organizations that have entrusted it with their third-party payment, including SMABTP and Audiens.

Our survey of the organizations offered by the optical portal is not published yet. At the counter, the customer’s Korelio card remains the most reliable check.

On the policyholder side, PRO BTP puts the number of Groupama and PRO BTP beneficiaries at 6 million. The Sévéane network, for its part, is closed. It selects a limited number of opticians per area. They are chosen based on a score covering the store, quality certification, lens traceability, equipment, services, lens prices, and CSR. Selected opticians commit to a maximum retail price for lenses, set according to the refractive error and the manufacturer.

Before its 2023 call for applications, Sévéane had listed 11 lens manufacturers. Acuité names them: BBGR-Nikon, Carl Zeiss Vision, Codir, Essilor, Hoya, Mega Optic, Novacel, Optiswiss, Rodenstock, Seiko, and Shamir. For the 2024 network, Acuité reports more than 5,000 optician applications accepted, 26% of them new partners. The current optical partnership contract covers 2024 to 2027, according to Sévéane’s optical page.

The right reflex: before entering anything, look at the customer’s Korelio third-party payment card. For opticians it carries the code “OPTI”, and this card is what confirms the policyholder’s coverage rights.

How do you access the Sévéane professional portal?

Access depends on your status: as a partner in the Sévéane network, you work on seveane.com; as an optician under agreement with Korelio outside the network, you work on korelio.com. Either way, you must first have joined the network or signed the Korelio optical agreement.

Outside the Sévéane network, an optician can indeed offer Korelio third-party payment by signing the agreement for delegation of payment of optical expenses. The Sévéane network adds partner status on top, with its commitments on lens prices. The steps are not the same.

Joining the Sévéane network

  1. Wait for a call for applications. The application is submitted on postulerseveane.com during a call, one application per store. The last one took place in fall 2023.
  2. Gather the documents. Professional liability insurance certificate, photos of the store, optical revenue certified by the accountant, AFNOR or Bureau Veritas quality certification, photos of the equipment, ADELI registration certificates, and diplomas.
  3. Get on the waiting list between two calls. Outside a call, Sévéane only approaches opticians on its waiting list. If a territory has no waiting list, a mini call for applications may take place.

Signing the Korelio optical agreement

The process starts from Korelio’s optician network agreement form. It goes like this:

  1. Fill out the membership application online. It asks for your health insurance number.
  2. Send the supporting documents. They are uploaded to the space indicated by email.
  3. Sign the agreement online. Signature comes after Korelio has reviewed the application.
  4. Create your account on korelio.com. A temporary password arrives by mail and must be changed at first login.

A signed agreement is not permanent. In July 2023, Korelio asked opticians to renew their agreement online from their subscriber area to keep third-party payment.

Logging in day to day

On korelio.com, you log in with the username and password of the store’s administrator account, then a code sent by email. The device can be marked as trusted for 30 days. Observed by our agents on the portal.

On seveane.com, logging in requires a username, a password, and a 6-digit code received by email.

The trap: on seveane.com, a rejected username displays “Service momentanément indisponible” (Service temporarily unavailable), the same message as a real outage. Before concluding there is an outage, double-check the username and password you entered.

How do you submit an optical coverage request on Sévéane?

The coverage request is made in the Korelio area, file by file, starting from the customer’s card. Once validated, it is billed from the same area with the “Facturer” button. This is the procedure Korelio describes on its “Signer une convention Korelio” (Sign a Korelio agreement) page.

Coverage approval (PEC) is the prior agreement by which the supplementary health insurer (mutuelle), or supplementary insurance (AMC), commits to the amount it will pay the optician. On Korelio, it is the status of the request, not the quote, that commits the organization.

  1. Check the customer’s card. Look for the code “OPTI” and the policyholder’s coverage rights on the Korelio third-party payment card.
  2. Log in to the right portal. korelio.com, or seveane.com if you are a partner in the Sévéane network, with the code received by email.
  3. Allow pop-up windows. Korelio requires the browser to accept them: allow the portal’s pop-up windows in your browser.
  4. Enter the request in the Korelio area. Enter the request from the customer’s card.
  5. Track the status. Until the request is accepted, the insurer has committed to nothing.
  6. Bill once the equipment is dispensed. The “Facturer” button on a validated coverage approval saves you from sending a paper invoice.

When these requests pile up on korelio.com and seveane.com, with an email code at every login, data entry quickly becomes the store’s bottleneck. This is what Granit does: agents submit coverage requests directly on the platforms’ portals, then send the status back to the team.

What do the statuses of a Sévéane coverage request mean?

Each request goes through a series of statuses, from entry to invoice. The table, compiled by our agents on the portal, gives their meaning and the action to take.

The status to watch is “Acceptée / validée” (Accepted / validated): that is when the insurer commits to the amount. Before that, a file marked “Estimée / saisie en cours” (Estimated / entry in progress) or “En instance” (Pending) commits nothing, even if the quote has been given to the customer.

One detail can be misleading when tracking an invoice. On Korelio, an e-transmitted invoice appears in the “Demandes de prises en charge” (Coverage requests) list, with the status “FACTUREE”. It is not in the list of optical coverage approvals. If you cannot find an invoiced file, look for it in that list first.

Finally, “Annulée” (Canceled) does not mean “Refusée” (Rejected). A canceled file is simply no longer active: you need to submit a new request if the equipment is still to be dispensed under third-party payment.

Stuck on Sévéane TP?

Before calling, check three places: the customer’s card, the status of the request, and the list where the invoice appears.

I cannot find the insurer in the list

Go back to the customer’s third-party payment card. It is what tells you whether the policyholder falls under Korelio, with the code “OPTI” for opticians. If the card is indeed a Korelio card, check that you are logged in to the right portal (korelio.com or seveane.com) and that your agreement is active. If the organization still cannot be found, call a Korelio management center. The five numbers are in the contact section below.

The coverage request is rejected

A “Refusée” status means there is no coverage approval as things stand. Read the reason displayed, correct what it points to, then submit the request again. Korelio does not publish a list of rejection reasons specific to optical care; if the reason remains unclear, call a Korelio management center.

It stays pending, with no answer

A file marked “En instance” is still under review. If the status is “Estimée / saisie en cours”, finish the entry. If a screen did not open, allow the portal’s pop-up windows in your browser. Korelio does not publish a turnaround time: if the customer is waiting for their equipment, call a Korelio management center.

The approval came through, but the payment does not arrive

First check that the invoice actually went out. After the equipment is dispensed, you must click “Facturer”. The file should then appear with the “FACTUREE” status in the “Demandes de prises en charge” list. An approval without an invoice is never paid. If the invoice did go out, call a Korelio management center with the file reference.

Keep the exact reason displayed by the portal: it is what tells you what to correct.

When and how does Sévéane pay the optician?

Korelio pays the optician: the third-party payment card guarantees reimbursement by Korelio, once the coverage approval is validated and billed from the professional portal. Korelio does not publish a payment timeline specific to optical care.

Payment therefore follows the invoice, not the approval. For a validated coverage approval, the “Facturer” button sends the invoice without any paper. The file then takes the “FACTUREE” status: all that remains is to track the bank transfer.

Korelio presents itself as the professional’s single point of contact. It is therefore Korelio you ask about a missing payment, whatever the customer’s organization. For day-to-day tracking, the most reliable method is to reconcile each bank transfer received against the files with the “FACTUREE” status, file by file. Our article on reconciling NOEMIE remittance files and bank transfers details this routine. The guide third-party payment for opticians, from coverage approval to collection places this step within the overall process.

With other operators, billing and payment rules change from one portal to the next. Compare, for example, with our page on Viamedis TP for opticians.

How do you contact Sévéane?

For third-party payment, your contact is Korelio. Its “Professionnels de santé” (Healthcare professionals) management centers are in Floirac, Créteil, Rouen, Sophia-Antipolis, and Wasquehal, listed on the “Contacter un centre de gestion” (Contact a management center) page.

For a first enrollment in third-party payment, use the membership application form for the Korelio optical agreement rather than the phone. Sévéane’s head office, at 8/10 rue d’Astorg in Paris according to the legal notice on seveane.com, is not the right contact for a coverage request file.

Before calling, have the customer’s card, the exact status of the file, and the reason displayed by the portal at hand. That way the management center can find the request.

faqItems.question: How does an optician access the Sévéane professional portal?
faqItems.answer: The professional portal is on korelio.com, or on seveane.com for partners in the Sévéane network. You must first be a partner in the network or have signed the Korelio optical agreement. In both cases, logging in requires a username, a password, and a code received by email.

faqItems.question: Which supplementary health insurers (mutuelles) go through Sévéane for optical third-party payment?
faqItems.answer: Sévéane third-party payment is managed by Korelio, PRO BTP’s services network. It covers PRO BTP and the organizations that have entrusted their third-party payment to Korelio, such as SMABTP and Audiens. Korelio publishes the list of these organizations on its partners page. At the counter, the customer’s Korelio card, with the code “OPTI” for opticians, remains the most reliable check.

faqItems.question: How do you submit an optical coverage request on Sévéane?
faqItems.answer: The request is made in the Korelio area, on korelio.com or on seveane.com for network partners, starting from the customer’s third-party payment card. The browser must accept pop-up windows. Once the coverage approval is validated and the equipment dispensed, the “Facturer” (Invoice) button sends the invoice with no paper.

faqItems.question: What do the statuses of a Sévéane coverage request mean (approved, pending, rejected)?
faqItems.answer: “Acceptée / validée” (Accepted / validated) means the supplementary insurer commits to the amount: you can dispense the equipment and then bill. “En instance” (Pending) means the file is still under review. “Refusée” (Rejected) means there is no coverage approval as things stand: read the reason, correct it, and submit the request again. “FACTUREE” (Invoiced) means the invoice has gone out and all that remains is to track the bank transfer.

faqItems.question: How does a healthcare professional contact Sévéane?
faqItems.answer: For third-party payment, your contact is Korelio, through its Healthcare professionals management centers in Floirac, Créteil, Rouen, Sophia-Antipolis, and Wasquehal. Their contact details are on the “Contacter un centre de gestion” (Contact a management center) page of korelio.com. For a first enrollment, use the membership application form for the Korelio optical agreement.

faqItems.question: How long does Sévéane take to pay the optician?
faqItems.answer: Korelio, which manages Sévéane third-party payment, does not publish a payment timeline specific to optical care. Payment follows the invoice, sent with the “Facturer” button once the coverage approval is validated. If a file with the “FACTUREE” status still has no bank transfer, call a Korelio management center with the file reference.
